findings.name: slit-lamp examination
findings.result: Right eye: inferonasal conjunctival injection with sectoral ciliary flush and limbitis; at the 4 o'clock position, small peripheral corneal infiltrates without epithelial defect or corneal staining; diffuse lamellar keratitis (grade I) beneath the SMILE cap margin, corresponding to the area of limbitis. Left eye: mild superficial punctate keratopathy.

findings.name: eyelid examination
findings.result: Both eyes: inspissated Meibomian glands and posterior marginal telangiectasias.

gold.reasoning: 1. Herpetic keratitis was considered as an infective cause of peripheral corneal inflammation—“Differential diagnosis considerations were given to various other possibilities including herpetic keratitis, peripheral stromal keratitis, and peripheral ulcerative keratitis including Mooren’s ulcer.” 2. Peripheral stromal keratitis was considered among the causes of peripheral infiltrates—“Differential diagnosis considerations were given to various other possibilities including herpetic keratitis, peripheral stromal keratitis, and peripheral ulcerative keratitis including Mooren’s ulcer.” 3. Peripheral ulcerative keratitis, including Mooren’s ulcer, was considered given the peripheral limbal involvement—“Differential diagnosis considerations were given to various other possibilities including herpetic keratitis, peripheral stromal keratitis, and peripheral ulcerative keratitis including Mooren’s ulcer.” 4. Ocular rosacea and keratitis associated with systemic vascular diseases or rheumatoid arthritis were also considered due to blepharitis signs—“In the setting of the appropriate patient past medical history or other applicable findings differential diagnoses could also have included ocular rosacea and keratitis associated with systemic vascular diseases or rheumatoid arthritis.” 5. All of these alternatives were excluded in favor of marginal keratitis because “Given the presence of limbitis and the absence of corneal staining or defect overlying the infiltrate, a diagnosis of marginal keratitis was made.”

leakage.reason: The slit-lamp result names 'diffuse lamellar keratitis' (a different, post-SMILE interface inflammation, as in the source); 'keratitis' is part of the gold name.
'Posterior marginal telangiectasias' refers to the eyelid margin, not the diagnosis; the word 'marginal' is part of the gold name.

notes: Index visit: the outpatient eye visit with 5 days of right-eye redness and 3 days of photophobia, pain and slight blurriness (s001-s010).
The slit-lamp findings of both eyes (s006-s009) are one record; the eyelid findings (s010) are a separate record so that a request about the lids or Meibomian glands is answered.
